GPK should be tracked as a mid-cap fiber/paperboard packaging candidate with explicit QSR cups, lids and food-container exposure, though restaurant exposure is diluted by broader packaging end markets.
REYN is a hypothesis-level restaurant-disposables adjacent name via Hefty Tableware; survival in later layers depends on proving meaningful commercial/catering/foodservice channel exposure.
AMCR is the public reference wrapper for former Berry Global foodservice packaging assets after the April 30, 2025 merger, but exposure purity is low relative to KRT and GPK.
Pactiv Evergreen/Novolex is a major private benchmark for this node but is no longer an investable standalone US-listed candidate after the April 1, 2025 Novolex transaction.

Next layer should verify pricing power for the node: resin/paper input cost pass-through, customer concentration, distributor dependence, import/tariff risk, sustainability regulation and whether foodservice volumes are actually growing.

KRT is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for the restaurant supplies/packaging/disposables node because its disclosures map directly to foodservice single-use products and it fits the $300M-$1B hunt range.

Foodservice packaging exposure has partly moved out of the public small/mid-cap universe: PTVE and Berry are no longer standalone listed equities after Novolex and Amcor transactions, reducing pure-play availability.
GPK and AMCR should be treated as reference anchors, not primary underfollowed alpha names, because their foodservice exposure is embedded inside broader packaging platforms.

PACK is a speculative shadow candidate for packaging automation and paper-based substitution; it should be removed in later layers unless restaurant/foodservice distributor or delivery/catering customer evidence appears.

Need a focused follow-up search on customer concentration and pricing power: KRT chain accounts, GPK foodservice revenue share, AMCR/Berry post-merger foodservice disclosure, resin/paperboard pass-through mechanisms, and sustainability regulation by state/local jurisdiction.

KRT is the cleanest underfollowed US-listed small-cap candidate for the restaurant packaging/disposables node because its filings directly describe disposable foodservice products used in restaurant settings.

GPK should be tracked as a mid-cap paperboard foodservice packaging supplier with QSR-linked cups, lids and containers, but restaurant exposure must be separated from broader consumer-packaging exposure.

REYN is a secondary/indirect candidate through Hefty Tableware and non-retail foodservice aluminum sales; require proof that restaurant/catering channels are material rather than primarily retail household demand.
PFGC is best used as a distributor-channel reference for disposables, cleaning and kitchen supplies sold into restaurants rather than as a pure packaging/disposables supplier.

Pactiv Evergreen would have been a major public foodservice-packaging reference, but it became private/delisted after the Novolex transaction closed on April 1, 2025; do not include PTVE in live public-universe screens.

KRT is the cleanest small-cap public pure-play candidate for restaurant packaging/disposables; prioritize in later layers for gross-margin durability, customer concentration, import exposure, and eco-compliant SKU pricing power.
GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard/QSR packaging candidate, but later layers must isolate foodservice exposure from broader CPG paperboard exposure.

Foodservice distributors such as PFGC and SYY are useful demand-signal anchors because their product categories include paper/disposables, equipment, smallwares, cleaning, and kitchen supplies, even when they are not manufacturers.

PTVE and Berry Global are no longer standalone public candidates after 2025 consolidation: PTVE was acquired by Novolex and delisted; Berry was acquired by Amcor. This reduces the number of direct public pure plays and may increase the importance of KRT and GPK as listed comparables.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expanded the public-company universe for restaurant packaging/disposables. The cleanest underfollowed direct exposure found is Karat Packaging (KRT), a small-cap manufacturer/distributor of disposable foodservice products used by restaurant chains and foodservice settings. Graphic Packaging (GPK) is a mid-cap paperboard packaging reference/underfollowed hybrid with disclosed cups, lids and food containers sold to foodservice companies and QSRs. Reynolds Consumer Products (REYN) is less directly tied to restaurants but has a Hefty Tableware disposable plates/bowls/cups/cutlery segment that may participate in catering/foodservice-adjacent demand, requiring channel verification. Amcor (AMCR), after acquiring Berry Global, is a large-cap context anchor for broad foodservice packaging scale, but its exposure is diluted across many packaging end markets. Pactiv Evergreen/Novolex is highly relevant to this node but was excluded from candidates because Pactiv Evergreen ceased to be a standalone public equity after the April 1, 2025 Novolex combination. Expanded the restaurant packaging/disposables node with a two-lane universe. The cleanest underfollowed direct exposure is Karat Packaging, a small-cap manufacturer/distributor of single-use foodservice disposables. Graphic Packaging and Amcor are larger reference/context names with foodservice packaging exposure but more diversified revenue bases.
